new: LEASE OF UNIT 7, FERNHILL TRADING ESTATE
This Lease is made on 1 October 2025 between Fernhill Estates Limited (the "Landlord") and Quillon Print Works Ltd (the "Tenant").
The Landlord lets the Property to the Tenant for a term of 10 years from and including the Term Commencement Date.
The Tenant shall pay the annual rent of £48,000 by unequal quarterly payments in advance on the usual quarter days.
The rent shall be reviewed on the fifth anniversary of the Term Commencement Date to the higher of the rent then payable and the open market rent.
The Tenant shall pay a service charge equal to a fair proportion of the costs reasonably incurred by the Landlord in providing the Services to the Estate.
The Tenant shall keep the Property in good and substantial repair and condition, except for damage caused by an Insured Risk.
The Tenant shall not make any structural alterations to the Property, and shall not make any other alterations without the consent of the Landlord, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld.
The Tenant shall use the Property only for purposes within Class B2 or Class B8 of the Use Classes Order.
The Tenant shall not assign the whole of the Property without the consent of the Landlord, and shall not assign or underlet part only of the Property.
The Landlord shall insure the Property against the Insured Risks for its full reinstatement cost, and the Tenant shall pay the Landlord on demand the insurance rent.
If the Property is damaged by an Insured Risk so as to be unfit for use, the rent shall be suspended until the Property is fit for use or for 3 years, whichever is shorter.
The Tenant may terminate this Lease on the fifth anniversary of the Term Commencement Date by giving the Landlord not less than 6 months' written notice, provided that it has paid all rent due.
The Landlord may re-enter the Property if any rent is unpaid for 21 days after becoming payable, or if the Tenant breaches any covenant in this Lease.
The Tenant shall provide a rent deposit of £12,000, to be held by the Landlord in a designated account and returned within 28 days after the end of the Term.
This Lease is governed by the law of England and Wales.

Nothing in this Agreement grants the receiving party any licence or other right in the Confidential Information, which remains the property of the disclosing party.
All Confidential Information is provided as is, and neither party gives any warranty as to its accuracy or completeness.
The obligations in this Agreement continue for a period of 3 years from the date of this Agreement, regardless of whether the parties enter into any further agreement.

new: SOFTWARE SUBSCRIPTION TERMS
These Terms apply to the subscription by the Customer to the Brightwater Scheduling platform supplied by Brightwater Systems Limited (the "Supplier").

The Supplier grants the Customer a non-exclusive, non-transferable right during the Subscription Term to permit the Authorised Users to use the Platform solely for the Customer's internal business operations.
The Customer shall not permit more than the number of Authorised Users stated in the Order Form to access the Platform at every time.
The Customer shall not copy, modify, reverse engineer or create derivative works of the Platform, except to the extent expressly permitted by law.
The Supplier shall use commercially reasonable endeavours to make the Platform available 99.5% of the time in each calendar month, excluding planned maintenance notified at least 48 hours in advance.
The Supplier shall provide support by email between 9am and 5pm on Business Days and shall respond to priority one incidents within 4 hours.
The Customer owns all Customer Data and grants the Supplier a licence to use it only to the extent necessary to provide the Platform and the support services.
The Supplier shall process personal data on behalf of the Customer only on the Customer's documented instructions and in accordance with the data processing terms in Schedule 2.
The Supplier shall back up Customer Data daily and retain each backup for 30 days.
The Customer shall pay the Subscription Fees annually in advance, and the Supplier may increase the Subscription Fees on each anniversary of the Start Date by not more than 5%.

The Subscription Term starts on the Start Date and continues for an initial period of 24 months, after which it renews automatically for successive periods of 12 months unless either party gives at least 90 days' notice before the end of the current period.
The Supplier may suspend access to the Platform if any undisputed Subscription Fees remain unpaid for more than 30 days after the due date.
On termination, the Supplier shall make the Customer Data available for export for 30 days, after which it may delete it.
The Supplier's aggregate liability in each contract year shall not exceed the Subscription Fees paid in that year.
These Terms are governed by the law of England and Wales.

These Terms apply to the subscription by the Customer to the Brightwater Scheduling platform supplied by Brightwater Systems Limited (the "Supplier").

The Supplier grants the Customer a non-exclusive, non-transferable right during the Subscription Term to permit the Authorised Users to use the Platform solely for the Customer's internal business operations.
The Customer shall not permit more than the number of Authorised Users stated in the Order Form to access the Platform at any time.
The Customer shall not copy, modify, reverse engineer or create derivative works of the Platform, except to the extent expressly permitted by law.
The Supplier shall use commercially reasonable endeavours to make the Platform available 99.5% of the time in each calendar month, excluding planned maintenance notified at least 48 hours in advance.
The Supplier shall provide support by email between 9am and 5pm on Business Days and shall respond to priority one incidents within 4 hours.
The Customer owns all Customer Data and grants the Supplier a licence to use it only to the extent necessary to provide the Platform and the support services.
The Supplier shall process personal data on behalf of the Customer only on the Customer's documented instructions and in accordance with the data processing terms in Schedule 2.
The Supplier shall back up Customer Data daily and retain each backup for 30 days.
The Customer shall pay the Subscription Fees annually in advance, and the Supplier may increase the Subscription Fees on each anniversary of the Start Date by not more than 5%.

Each party shall comply with all applicable anti-bribery and anti-corruption laws, including the Bribery Act 2010, and shall maintain adequate procedures to prevent bribery by persons associated with it.

The Subscription Term starts on the Start Date and continues for an initial period of 24 months, after which it renews automatically for successive periods of 12 months unless either party gives at least 90 days' notice before the end of the current period.
The Supplier may suspend access to the Platform if any undisputed Subscription Fees remain unpaid for more than 30 days after the due date.
On termination, the Supplier shall make the Customer Data available for export for 30 days, after which it may delete it.
The Supplier's aggregate liability in each contract year shall not exceed the Subscription Fees paid in that year.
These Terms are governed by the law of England and Wales.

new: CONSULTANCY SERVICES AGREEMENT

This Agreement is dated 14 July 2025 and is made between Larkspur Retail Group plc of 20 Mill Lane, Bristol BS1 4XY (the "Client") and Tessellate Data Consulting Ltd of 5 Quay Street, Leeds LS2 7AB (the "Consultant").
The Consultant shall provide the data migration and reporting services described in Schedule 1 (the "Services") from the Commencement Date until the end of the Term.
The Consultant shall perform the Services with reasonable skill and care, in accordance with good industry practice and in compliance with all applicable laws.
The Client shall provide the Consultant with access to its premises, systems and personnel as reasonably required for the performance of the Services.
The Client shall pay the Consultant a fee of £1,200 per day for each day on which the Services are performed, together with any reasonable expenses approved in advance by the Client.
The Consultant shall invoice the Client monthly in arrears, and the Client shall pay each valid invoice within 30 days of receipt.
If the Client fails to pay any amount by the due date, the Consultant can charge interest on the overdue amount at the rate of 4% per year above the Bank of England base rate.

All intellectual property rights in the deliverables created by the Consultant in performing the Services shall vest in the Client on creation, and the Consultant hereby assigns those rights to the Client.
The Consultant shall maintain professional indemnity insurance with a limit of not less than £2,000,000 for each claim throughout the Term and for 6 years afterwards.
Neither party's total liability under this Agreement shall exceed an amount equal to the fees paid in the 12 months before the event giving rise to the claim.
Nothing in this Agreement limits either party's liability for death or personal injury caused by its negligence, or for fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation.
Either party may terminate this Agreement by giving not less than 60 days' written notice to the other party.
Either party may terminate this Agreement with immediate effect if the other party commits a material breach which is not remedied within 14 days of a written request to do so.
On termination, the Client shall pay the Consultant for all Services performed up to the date of termination, and the Consultant shall return all property of the Client in its possession.
The Consultant is an independent contractor and nothing in this Agreement creates a relationship of employment, partnership or agency between the parties.
This Agreement is governed by the law of England and Wales.

This Agreement is dated 14 July 2025 and is made between Larkspur Retail Group plc of 20 Mill Lane, Bristol BS1 4XY (the "Client") and Tessellate Data Consulting Ltd of 5 Quay Street, Leeds LS2 7AB (the "Consultant").
The Consultant shall provide the data migration and reporting services described in Schedule 1 (the "Services") from the Commencement Date until the end of the Term.
The Consultant shall perform the Services with reasonable skill and care, in accordance with good industry practice and in compliance with all applicable laws.
The Client shall provide the Consultant with access to its premises, systems and personnel as reasonably required for the performance of the Services.
The Client shall pay the Consultant a fee of £1,200 per day for each day on which the Services are performed, together with any reasonable expenses approved in advance by the Client.
The Consultant shall invoice the Client monthly in arrears, and the Client shall pay each valid invoice within 30 days of receipt.
If the Client fails to pay any amount by the due date, the Consultant may charge interest on the overdue amount at the rate of 4% per year above the Bank of England base rate.

All intellectual property rights in the deliverables created by the Consultant in performing the Services shall vest in the Client on creation, and the Consultant hereby assigns those rights to the Client.
The Consultant shall maintain professional indemnity insurance with a limit of not less than £2,000,000 for each claim throughout the Term and for 6 years afterwards.
Neither party's total liability under this Agreement shall exceed an amount equal to the fees paid in the 12 months before the event giving rise to the claim.
Either party may terminate this Agreement by giving not less than 60 days' written notice to the other party.
Either party may terminate this Agreement with immediate effect if the other party commits a material breach which is not remedied within 14 days of a written request to do so.
On termination, the Client shall pay the Consultant for all Services performed up to the date of termination, and the Consultant shall return all property of the Client in its possession.
The Consultant is an independent contractor and nothing in this Agreement creates a relationship of employment, partnership or agency between the parties.
This Agreement is governed by the law of England and Wales.

new: SIDE LETTER IN RELATION TO THE SHAREHOLDERS' AGREEMENT OF ORBITAL KITCHEN LTD
To: Priya Fernando, Founder
Dear Priya,

We refer to the shareholders' agreement dated 2 February 2025 between Orbital Kitchen Ltd (the "Company") and its shareholders (the "Shareholders' Agreement"). Terms defined in the Shareholders' Agreement have the same meaning in this letter.
The Company confirms that the Founder shall be entitled to appoint one director to the Board for so long as she holds at least 10% of the Shares in issue.
The Founder shall be a Good Leaver if she ceases to be an employee by reason of death, serious ill health or permanent disability, or if she is dismissed without Cause.
The Founder shall be a Bad Leaver if her employment is terminated by the Company for Cause, or if she resigns within 24 months of the date of the Shareholders' Agreement.
If the Founder is a Bad Leaver, she shall be required to transfer all of her Shares at the lower of their nominal value and their fair market value.
If the Founder is a Good Leaver, she shall be required to transfer only her Unvested Shares, at their fair market value.
The Shares held by the Founder shall vest in equal monthly instalments over a period of 48 months from the date of the Shareholders' Agreement, subject to a cliff of 12 months.
The investors agree that the Founder may transfer up to 5% of her Shares to a family trust, provided that the trustees first sign a deed of adherence.
This letter is supplemental to the Shareholders' Agreement, and in the event of any conflict between them, this letter shall prevail.
This letter must terminate automatically on the earlier of an Exit and the date on which the Founder ceases to hold any Shares.
This letter is governed by the law of England and Wales.
Yours sincerely,
For and on behalf of ORBITAL KITCHEN LTD.

This letter shall terminate automatically on the earlier of an Exit and the date on which the Founder ceases to hold any Shares.
This letter is governed by the law of England and Wales.
Yours sincerely,
